blocks.title: How does the page description get into viz?
blocks.body:
Three options.

**Heredoc on stdin** — one bash call, nothing left on disk. The quoted delimiter means no shell interpolation, so backticks and `$` in the JSON are safe.

**Temp file** — the model writes the JSON with its file tool, then runs `viz <file>`. Two tool calls, and litter to clean up, but the JSON is inspectable afterwards.

**Argument** — `viz '{...}'`. Simplest to type, but long JSON on a command line hits argument length limits and quoting problems.

blocks.title: What does viz print back?
blocks.body:
The output is read by a model, not parsed by a program.

**Compact lines** (`q1: Heredoc on stdin`) are cheap and unambiguous.

**JSON** is machine-readable but costs more tokens and invites the model to re-emit it.
options: JSON behind a flag, lines by default

blocks.title: How does the model learn the block schema?
blocks.body:
viz is a CLI, so there is no automatic schema discovery the way an MCP server would have.

**Inline in each skill** — every skill carries its own example. Duplicated, but each one is tuned to that skill.

**A shared reference file** the skills point at. One source of truth, one more file to read.

**`viz --help`** — the model runs it when unsure. Zero standing cost, but an extra round trip.
